  "title": "Forced Proximity",
  "description": "Reusable adult forced-proximity engine in which {{user}} and adult {{char}} unexpectedly spend an extended period alone or in unusually close proximity because they are locked in, stranded, sheltering, delayed, assigned together, sharing limited accommodation, or otherwise unable to separate normally. Detailed presets vary cause, genuine lock versus practical constraint, duration, starting relationship, physical space and privacy, resources, sleeping arrangements, interaction dynamics, rescue/outside contact, consent and safety boundaries, emotional trajectory, workplace variants, travel/hotel/one-bed variants, strong openings, cross-series bridges, and outcomes.",
  "source_version": "1.2",
  "bible": {
    "series": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible I",

    "category": "Setting & Slice of Life",
    "source_date": "2026-09-21"

  "summary": "Adult {{user}} and adult {{char}} are unexpectedly kept together far longer or more closely than normal. They may be locked in a room, shut inside a building after security closes it, sheltering from severe weather, dealing with a hotel booking error or one-bed room, stranded by travel disruption, stuck in an elevator, paired by an adult party game, working an overnight assignment, or trapped in a storage/equipment room. The source treats physical confinement, practical inability to leave, duration, privacy, resources, sleeping arrangements, rescue, starting relationship, and possible personal change as separate variables.",
  "core_premise": "The engine is unusual closeness caused by circumstance rather than entitlement. The important questions are why separation is difficult, how long it lasts, whether the adults are truly locked in or merely better off staying, what space/resources/privacy they have, what their relationship was before the event, and what interaction naturally follows. Forced proximity can create friendship, respect, annoyance, vulnerability, attraction, closure, or no meaningful change. It never creates romantic or sexual consent.",
  "setup": "Begin at or just after the moment the proximity becomes unavoidable: a door will not open, security confirms a delay, severe-weather advice arrives, transport is cancelled, a hotel reveals the room error, an elevator stops, the party game begins, an overnight assignment is extended, or the pair realize they may be waiting until morning. Establish the practical ground truth, expected duration if known, available communication, and enough starting relationship context to make the interaction meaningful. Do not pre-write {{user}}’s attraction, sleeping choice, touch, confession, consent, frustration, rescue decision, or future relationship.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Why {{user}} and {{char}} are stuck together or unable to separate normally.",
    "Whether the constraint is a literal locked space, external danger, unavailable transport, work obligation, accommodation shortage, or merely the least-bad practical option.",
    "How long the situation is expected to last and how that estimate changes.",
    "What relationship the adults had before the event.",
    "How much physical room, visual privacy, bathroom privacy, and personal space are available.",
    "What food, water, power, communication, bedding, clothing, entertainment, and work resources are available.",
    "Whether sleeping arrangements matter and what alternatives exist.",
    "Who outside knows where they are and what rescue, staff, transport, or security updates are available.",
    "What practical problems they have to solve together.",
    "Whether boredom, stress, professional duty, bad weather, or simple inconvenience shapes the conversation.",
    "Whether either adult already has attraction, resentment, friendship, history, or professional dependence.",
    "What changes between them, if anything, after hours of unusual proximity.",
    "Whether the circumstance ends earlier or later than expected.",
    "Whether the setting is workplace, travel, hotel, student, residential, social, or outdoor shelter.",
    "Whether the eventual outcome is friendship, respect, irritation, attraction, closure, a future invitation, or no change."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Preserve the defining hook: adult {{user}} and adult {{char}} unexpectedly spend an extended period alone or in unusually close proximity.",
    "If Locked Room is selected, establish a credible mechanical, administrative, or situational reason for the lock and a plausible expected exit/rescue path.",
    "If Security Locked the Building is selected, distinguish safe after-hours lock-in from an active emergency that requires evacuation.",
    "If Storm Shelter is selected, prioritize real safety and weather conditions over romantic framing.",
    "If Hotel Booking Error is selected, preserve realistic attempts to seek another room, rollaway bed, sofa, refund, or alternate accommodation before treating room-sharing as fixed.",
    "If One Bed is selected, keep all reasonable sleeping options open and never treat one bed as consent to physical intimacy.",
    "If Travel Disruption is selected, make the transport problem and alternatives materially relevant.",
    "If Elevator Breakdown is selected, use normal communication/rescue procedures and avoid inventing unnecessary danger.",
    "If Party Game is selected, participation remains voluntary and either adult can end the game if uncomfortable.",
    "If Overnight Work Assignment is selected, preserve legitimate work purpose, compensation/policy context where relevant, and professional boundaries.",
    "If Locked Equipment / Storage Room is selected, preserve realistic ventilation, safety, access, and communication constraints.",
    "Always distinguish physically locked confinement from practical inability to leave and from voluntary choice to stay.",
    "Do not use the circumstance itself as evidence of attraction or consent.",
    "Do not pre-write {{user}}’s attraction, touch, dialogue, sleeping choice, confession, romance, sex, rescue behavior, or future decision.",
    "Allow fully platonic, professional, irritated, comedic, reflective, or unchanged trajectories.",
    "If a selected preset narrows cause, duration, relationship, privacy, sleeping setup, work context, travel context, or outcome, preserve it while varying remaining axes."

  "guardrails": [
    "All romantic or sexual participants are adults.",
    "Physical confinement, weather, transport failure, one bed, shared shelter, fatigue, fear, and privacy loss do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Do not deliberately sabotage doors, locks, lifts, vehicles, phones, bookings, transport, weather information, or rescue in order to trap another person.",
    "Do not hide an available safe exit, rescue message, alternate room, or transportation option to prolong proximity.",
    "Do not block or physically prevent an adult from leaving once safe exit is possible.",
    "Serious emergencies prioritize safety, evacuation, first aid, and professional responders over relationship beats.",
    "Do not romanticize unsafe sheltering during fire, flood, storm, structural danger, medical crisis, or other real emergencies.",
    "One-bed scenarios must preserve separate sleeping alternatives where reasonably available and explicit agreement for any shared sleeping space.",
    "A sleeping, intoxicated, medically impaired, or severely exhausted person cannot be treated as consenting to new sexual contact.",
    "Preserve bathroom, changing, clothing, and personal-space privacy as much as circumstances allow.",
    "For workplace variants, managerial, trainer, assessor, roster, pay, and employment power must remain separate from personal consent.",
    "Do not treat party games as contracts for kissing, sex, nudity, or other intimacy.",
    "Do not force confessions, reconciliation, dating, sex, or emotional disclosure merely because the pair cannot leave.",
    "Do not use cosmetic changes of room, hotel, vehicle, storm, or job as the sole basis for supposedly different ideas."
